notes:
Task and constraints: Return every structurally distinct binary search tree containing values 1 through n, with n at most 8; the number of outputs grows as a Catalan number.
Idea: build(lo, hi) chooses each value in the interval as a root, recursively obtains every left tree from lo through value-1 and every right tree from value+1 through hi, then pairs each left result with each right result and appends the new root to out.
Technique and why it applies: Recursive decomposition by root value works because a BST's left subtree must contain smaller values and its right subtree larger values; combining all valid subtrees enumerates all shapes.
Invariant: Every tree returned by build(lo, hi) uses exactly the interval's values once and satisfies the BST ordering around every chosen root.
Edge cases: When lo > hi, [None] supplies an empty child so a leaf can be assembled. For n=1, the result contains one node with two empty children. For n=3, choosing 2 yields left child 1 and right child 3, while roots 1 and 3 generate the other shapes.
Complexity: With C_n Catalan-number output trees, time is O(n * C_n) because each output tree has n nodes; space is O(n * C_n) for the returned trees plus O(n) recursion depth.
complexity_reason: The recursion enumerates every root split and every Cartesian product of left and right subtree lists, storing all generated trees.

notes:
Task and constraints: Enumerate all distinct BST structures containing values 1 through n, where n <= 8 and the output count grows rapidly with n.
Idea: generateTrees delegates to build(1,n). build returns a list containing null for an empty interval; otherwise it tries each v as root, recursively builds lists for [lo,v-1] and [v+1,hi], and adds a newly allocated TreeNode for every left-right pair.
Technique and why it applies: Divide-and-conquer over the root value enforces BST ordering automatically, and the nested loops combine every valid left shape with every valid right shape.
Invariant: Each nonempty list entry returned from build(lo,hi) is rooted at one chosen value and has only smaller interval values on the left and larger interval values on the right.
Edge cases: lo > hi returns a one-element list containing null, allowing leaf nodes to be created. With n=1, one TreeNode is returned. The implementation's generic List<TreeNode> and null children represent empty subtrees; recursion depth can reach n, though n is capped at 8.
Complexity: With C_n Catalan-number output trees, time is O(n * C_n) because each output tree has n nodes; space is O(n * C_n) for the returned trees plus O(n) recursion depth.
complexity_reason: Each interval tries every possible root and stores a new TreeNode for every pair from the recursively generated left and right lists.

notes:
Task and constraints: Decide whether s3 interleaves s1 and s2 without changing either source string's character order; the lengths can be up to 100 each.
Idea: Reject immediately when m+n differs from len(s3). Otherwise dp[i][j] records whether the first i characters of s1 and first j of s2 can form the first i+j characters of s3. Start with dp[0][0] true and propagate from the upper or left cell when the matching source character equals s3[i+j-1].
Technique and why it applies: Two-dimensional dynamic programming combines the only two possible ways to form a prefix: take its final character from s1 or from s2.
Invariant: A true dp[i][j] always corresponds to a valid interleaving of exactly those two source prefixes, with their internal order preserved.
Edge cases: Unequal total lengths return false before allocating dp. Two empty source strings and empty s3 leave dp[0][0] true. If the next target character matches both source tails, either true predecessor can establish the state.
Complexity: The nested loops fill (m+1)(n+1) cells, giving O(mn) time and O(mn) space for the Boolean table.
complexity_reason: The code visits every cell of an (m+1) by (n+1) Boolean table and stores that entire table.
